concept.title: How to Use Self-Referential Content: A Guide for Technical Writers Working with Software Engineers

conbody.p: This topic demonstrates how self-referential DITA content can be used as a living example and template for technical writers collaborating with software engineers.

section.title: Why Use Self-Referential Content?
section.p: Self-referential topics explain their own structure and maintenance, making onboarding and handoff easier for both writers and engineers. They serve as both documentation and meta-documentation.

ul.li: Use self-referential topics as templates for new documentation.
Encourage engineers to update the how-to-update and how-to-extend sections when making changes.
Document code samples and API references using DITA reference and task topics, linking to self-referential examples.
Use conref and keyref for shared warnings, standards, and terminology.
Validate all changes with the DITA-OT validator and review output in both HTML and PDF.

ol.li: Copy a self-referential topic as a starting point for new documentation.
Replace the instructional content with project-specific information, keeping the meta-sections updated.
Link to shared content (e.g., safety warnings) using conref.
Review with both technical writers and engineers to ensure clarity and accuracy.

section.title: How to Update This Guide
section.p: Edit the sections above to reflect new best practices or lessons learned from real projects. Add new sections for advanced collaboration tips as needed.
